Create an evaluation suite for our MCP server that wraps the company wiki (search, read pages, list spaces).
expected_behavior: creates ~10 independent, read-only questions grounded in real content, each with a single stable verifiable answer and a specified answer format
makes questions complex (multi-hop, paraphrased so keyword search alone cannot shortcut them) and diverse in answer modality
verifies every answer by solving it with the tools before accepting it into the suite
runs the suite through an agent harness against the live server and reports accuracy, tool-call counts, latency, and token usage
reads failing transcripts to locate confusion and feeds fixes back into tool descriptions/schemas, keeping a held-out subset to detect overfitting

cases.prompt: Our coding agent keeps calling jira_search when it should call jira_get_issue. Diagnose and fix the selection problem.
expected_behavior: treats tool selection as a measurable classification problem with an offline eval set of prompt-to-expected-tool pairs
checks the two descriptions for overlap/ambiguity and rewrites them with disjoint when-to-use guidance rather than only prompt-tuning the agent
re-runs the selection eval after the description change and compares accuracy
recommends description-overlap detection in CI so regressions are caught on future edits

cases.prompt: Before we tag v1.0 of our MCP server, verify it is protocol-correct.
expected_behavior: exercises every tool/resource/prompt in MCP Inspector including at least one error path per tool and empty-result behavior
runs the official conformance suite against the server and triages failures
tests on the transports actually shipped (stdio and/or Streamable HTTP), not just one
gates the release on build + conformance + eval accuracy, not on unit tests alone

cases.prompt: Load test our remote MCP server before launch.
expected_behavior: drives realistic JSON-RPC tools/call POSTs against the MCP endpoint with the required Accept headers, not just GET /health
sets explicit thresholds (error rate, p95 latency) that fail the run
uses a representative tool mix including at least one expensive tool, and watches session/auth behavior under concurrency where applicable
reports results with the limiting resource identified rather than a bare pass
